newsitem.title: JAPAN: Asian traders see LME copper remaining volatile.
newsitem.headline: Asian traders see LME copper remaining volatile.

text.p: Copper prices on the London Metal Exchange (LME) are likely to remain volatile in technically driven trade against the backdrop of a large backwardation, Asian traders said on Wednesday.
"Prices are going to show wide swings on technical short-covering. The backwardation is likely to remain wide until the end of this month," said a trader at one of Japan's leading trading houses.
He said three-month copper was unlikely to breach resistance at $2,355, while short-covering by funds and South Korea's LG Metals Corp was expected to support the red metal.

A document of LG Futures Co Ltd, broker for LG Metals, obtained by Reuters in London showed LG's open positions included copper shorts of 105,475 tonnes and aluminium longs of 125,900 tonnes as of June 20.
At 0215 GMT, benchmark three-month copper was quoted at $2,281/$2,286 a tonne, little changed from $2,280/$2,284 at 1800 GMT on Tuesday.

Copper gave up $37 in London overnight to finish the afternoon kerb at $2,278, breaking below the key $2,300 level, while the cash-to-threes backwardation remained at $250/$255 after flaring by $100 during Third Wednesday pricing on Monday.
But traders agreed the metal would look downwards in August when the backwardation was expected to narrow.
"With the wide backwardation, lots of metal will be delivered to warehouses, yet we cannot expect much buying interest from users," one trader said.
Aluminium, on the other hand, faced technical selling, although its fundamentals looked much stronger than those of the flagship copper contract, traders said.
At 0215 GMT, three-month aluminium was quoted at $1,562/$1,566 a tonne, compared with $1,564/$1,567 at 1800 GMT on Tuesday and its Tuesday kerb close at $1,563.
Three-month zinc was quoted at at $1,490/$1,495 a tonne, versus $1,492 at 1800 GMT and $1,491 at the Tuesday kerb close.
Traders said zinc had to go through a consolidation, with a possible downside move to $1,420, before resuming its upward trend amid tightness in the physical market.

"China's big Zhuzhou smelter seems to have a large short position around September. Of course, as a smelter it can produce more metal, but it seems to be having difficulties getting enough ore," said one trader.
